categoryId > 0: query = (from o in query join oi in _orderItemRepository.Table on o.Id equals oi.OrderId join p in _productRepository.Table on oi.ProductId equals p.Id join pc in _productCategoryRepository.Table on p.Id equals pc.ProductId where pc.CategoryId == categoryId select o).Distinct();

reports.aggregation: Per date bucket (result = grouped orders): OrderCount = result.Count(); OrderShippingExclTaxSum = result.Sum(o => o.OrderShippingExclTax); OrderPaymentFeeExclTaxSum = result.Sum(o => o.PaymentMethodAdditionalFeeExclTax); OrderTaxSum = result.Sum(o => o.OrderTax); OrderTotalSum = result.Sum(o => o.OrderTotal); OrderRefundedAmountSum = result.Sum(o => o.RefundedAmount); OrderTotalCost = orderItems.Sum(oi => (decimal?)oi.OriginalProductCost * oi.Quantity) where orderItems is the UNFILTERED order-item set for every order in the bucket. Final Profit = OrderTotalSum - OrderShippingExclTaxSum - OrderPaymentFeeExclTaxSum - OrderTaxSum - OrderRefundedAmountSum - Convert.ToDecimal(OrderTotalCost). All revenue/tax/shipping/refund figures use ORDER-level columns (o.OrderTotal, o.OrderTax, etc.), never SUM(oi.PriceExclTax) or any other item-level column.
reports.group_by: oq.CreatedOnUtc.AddMinutes(utcOffsetInMinutes).AddDays(1 - oq.CreatedOnUtc.AddMinutes(utcOffsetInMinutes).Day).Date -- i.e. the first day of the order's create-month, in the CURRENT SERVER TIME ZONE offset (utcOffsetInMinutes = userTimeZone.BaseUtcOffset.TotalMinutes; note this is the *server's* configured time zone via IDateTimeHelper, not necessarily the requesting admin's own zone), truncated to a Date
reports.ordering: orderby orderItem.SummaryDate descending (most recent month first)
reports.limit: None inherent to the method (pageSize defaults to int.MaxValue); the admin grid applies AdminAreaSettings.DefaultGridPageSize (installed default = 15, see src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Installation/InstallRequiredData.cs:1417) via searchModel.SetGridPageSize() in PrepareSalesSummarySearchModelAsync
reports.notes: CRITICAL: when any of categoryId/manufacturerId/productId/vendorId/billingCountryId is set, the filter only decides WHICH ORDERS qualify (an order qualifies if it contains at least one matching item) -- it does NOT restrict the summed amounts to that item's share. OrderTotalSum, OrderTaxSum, OrderShippingExclTaxSum, OrderRefundedAmountSum are always the FULL order totals, including revenue from products/categories/manufacturers/vendors OUTSIDE the filter, as long as the order also contains one matching line. A reimplementation that assumes 'Sales by category' sums only that category's line items will overstate/misattribute revenue. The cost component (OrderTotalCost) independently re-queries ALL order items of the qualifying orders (not just filtered ones) via 'result.Any(x => x.Id == oi.OrderId)', compounding the same issue for the Profit figure. Default admin OrderStatusIds/PaymentStatusIds are null (no restriction) unless the admin explicitly picks specific statuses in the UI -- Pending and Cancelled orders ARE included by default. Date range end is adjusted by the factory (endDateValue = ...AddDays(1)) to make the End Date inclusive; the service's own predicate is a plain '<=' comparison. GroupByOptions.Month = value 2 in the enum; 'Sales summary by month' is not a separate method, just this method called with groupBy: GroupByOptions.Month.

reports.notes: There is NO dedicated 'Sales by Category' report screen or method that groups revenue BY category (i.e. one row per category with its own revenue sum in a single query). categoryId is only usable as a single-value FILTER on the generic Sales Summary screen (one category at a time, requiring N separate report runs to build an N-category table). Crucially -- see report #1's notes -- this filter only determines which ORDERS qualify (contains >=1 item in the category); the summed OrderTotal/OrderTax/etc. still include the FULL order value, including line items from OTHER categories in the same order. A reimplementation that computes true per-category revenue (sum of only that category's line-item amounts) will NOT match nopCommerce's 'Sales Summary filtered by category' output.

joins: Address joined on Order.BillingAddressId == Address.Id (always, GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync line 309)
OrderItem/Product/ProductWarehouseInventory joined only if vendorId/productId/warehouseId supplied (not used by this caller)
OrderNote joined only if orderNotes supplied (not used by this caller)
optional_filters: osIds: [ (int)os ] -- exactly one OrderStatus per call; OrderAverageReportAsync is invoked once each for Pending, Processing, Complete, Cancelled (OrderModelFactory.cs lines 1775-1778)

5 periods computed per status via 5 separate GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync calls, each with a different startTimeUtc lower bound and NO upper bound: today (midnight today), this week (start of week per CultureInfo.CurrentCulture.DateTimeFormat.FirstDayOfWeek), this month (1st of month), this year (Jan 1), all-time (no startTimeUtc at all)
reports.aggregation: Per (status, period) cell: CountOrders = result.Count(); SumOrders (i.e. 'order value' shown) = result.Sum(o => o.OrderTotal) -- despite the name 'Average order value', this is NOT divided by count anywhere in the traced code -- it is a raw SUM of o.OrderTotal, not an average. (SumShippingExclTax, SumTax, SumRefundedAmount, OrderPaymentFeeExclTaxSum are also computed by GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync but are not surfaced by OrderAverageReportLineSummary/this widget.)
reports.group_by: 4 status rows x 5 period columns = 20 cells, each its own independent query (no single GROUP BY query)
reports.ordering: Fixed row order: Pending, Processing, Complete, Cancelled
reports.notes: Despite its name, this report displays SUMS, not averages/means -- 'Average order value' would conventionally mean SumOrders / CountOrders, but no division occurs anywhere in OrderAverageReportAsync, GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync, or the model mapping; the raw sum is passed straight through as e.g. SumTodayOrders. This is a strong candidate for a reimplementation to silently 'fix' by adding an actual average calculation that the source does not perform. Each of the 20 cells is a fully independent database round trip (no batching), all filtered only by !o.Deleted, one OrderStatus, and an open-ended start date -- there is no storeId or vendorId scoping anywhere in this report, so it is always store-wide/vendor-wide.

reports.source: No dedicated report exists. RefundedAmount is summed only as one COMPONENT inside broader aggregations: src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Orders/OrderReportService.cs, method GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync, line 355 (SumRefundedAmount), reused by OrderAverageReportAsync (lines 387-442), ProfitReportAsync (lines 923-1009), and SalesSummaryReportAsync's OrderRefundedAmountSum (lines 581/596/611)
reports.aggregation: SumRefundedAmount / OrederRefundedAmountSum / OrderRefundedAmountSum = result.Sum(o => o.RefundedAmount) -- always an ORDER-level column (the cumulative amount refunded against that order), never derived from a separate Refund/RefundTransaction entity
reports.notes: There is no admin screen whose sole purpose is 'total refunds issued'; RefundedAmount only appears as a subtracted term inside the Sales Summary 'Profit' formula (report #1/#2) and as a raw field on OrderAverageReportLine (unused by the surfaced 'Average order value' widget, which only shows SumOrders per cell -- see report #16 notes). A reimplementation that invents a standalone 'Refund totals' report method would not correspond to anything in this codebase; reporting null rather than fabricating one, per instructions.

reports.source: No dedicated report exists. OrderTax is summed only as one COMPONENT inside broader aggregations: src/Libraries/Nop.Services/Orders/OrderReportService.cs, method GetOrderAverageReportLineAsync, line 353 (OrderTaxSum), and SalesSummaryReportAsync, lines 579/594/609 (OrderTaxSum)
reports.aggregation: OrderTaxSum = result.Sum(o => o.OrderTax) -- ORDER-level tax column (the order's total tax amount as stored at checkout time), never a recomputation from tax rates/line items
reports.notes: Like Refund totals, tax collected only surfaces as an intermediate subtracted term in the Sales Summary 'Profit' calculation (report #1/#2) and as a formatted 'Tax' column on each SalesSummaryReportLine row (SalesSummaryReportAsync line 632, formatted via _priceFormatter.FormatPriceAsync) -- there IS a visible per-period Tax column on the Sales Summary grid, so 'tax collected per day/week/month' can be read off that report, but there is no separate 'Tax Collected' report screen or method distinct from Sales Summary. Reporting null as a standalone method per instructions, while noting the SalesSummaryReportLine.Tax column as the closest concrete artifact.

reports.source: No implementation in OrderReportService.cs or CustomerReportService.cs. Closest artifact is src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Areas/Admin/Controllers/OrderController.cs, method LoadOrderStatistics, starting at line 2684, which backs the dashboard '_OrderStatistics' chart (src/Presentation/Nop.Web/Areas/Admin/Views/Home/_OrderStatistics.cshtml) -- but it uses IOrderService.SearchOrdersAsync (a different service, not provided) and counts orders, not revenue.
reports.aggregation: value = (await _orderService.SearchOrdersAsync(createdFromUtc: ..., createdToUtc: ..., pageIndex: 0, pageSize: 1, getOnlyTotalCount: true)).TotalCount.ToString() -- this is an ORDER COUNT per day/month bucket (via a TotalCount side-channel of a paged search, one query per bucket), NOT a sum of any revenue/OrderTotal column
reports.group_by: Client requests one of 'week' (8 daily buckets), 'month' (31 daily buckets over ~30 days), or 'year' (13 monthly buckets) via a period parameter; each bucket triggers its own independent SearchOrdersAsync call (no single GROUP BY query)
reports.ordering: Chronological, oldest bucket first (loop increments the date forward)
reports.notes: This is a count-of-orders-over-time chart, not a revenue trend, and it is implemented via IOrderService (OrderController.cs), not IOrderReportService/ICustomerReportService -- outside the scope of the two named report services and not a true match for 'Daily revenue trend' semantically (counts orders, doesn't sum money) or organizationally (wrong service). A vendor-context admin gets an empty chart entirely: 'if (await _workContext.GetCurrentVendorAsync() != null) return Content(string.Empty);' (lines 2686-2688). Reporting null for a same-service implementation per instructions, while flagging this adjacent artifact so it isn't silently missed.
